boxes.text: Define the exact flagship scientific question in one sentence.
Define the weakest defensible GMI core claim.
Define the strongest eventual GMI claim.
Define explicit forbidden claims at each evidence level.
Replace ambiguous uses of `obligation` in paper-facing theory with academically grounded terminology (`task`, `behavioral specification`, `requirement`, etc.) while preserving exact legacy mappings.
Define `behavioral specification` formally and prove its relation to existing obligation objects.
Define architecture-prior-free derivation formally.
Prove why literally assumption-free/prior-free derivation is impossible or ill-posed.
Define what counts as an architectural prior, representation prior, operator prior, search prior, ecological prior, and evaluation prior.
Create a prior-disclosure schema for every derivation experiment.
Define evidence levels for every GMI claim.

Define a maturity ladder, e.g. M0 concept → M1 theorem → M2 exact witness → M3 architecture-prior-free recovery → M4 frozen held-out prediction → M5 independent replication → M6 real-scale prospective validation.
Re-score every major existing GMI result on the maturity ladder.
Require every result to state scope, quantifiers, assumptions, falsifiers, strongest parents, and forbidden extrapolations.
Establish an explicit rule that checklist closure never implies ontological completeness.
Inventory every GMI theorem, lemma, proposition, definition, algorithm, experiment, receipt, and claimed law on `main`.
Build a machine-readable theorem dependency graph.
Identify circular dependencies.
Identify duplicated results under different terminology.
Identify claims whose theorem names are stronger than their actual quantifiers.
Identify proofs that rely on finite enumeration where an analytic proof is possible.
Identify analytic claims supported only by computation.
Identify computational claims with no independent implementation.
Identify assumptions introduced after observing outcomes.
Identify search grammars that encode the target morphology.
Identify cost models that structurally force the claimed winner.
Identify hidden architecture macros or privileged operators.
Identify hidden independence/iid/stationarity assumptions.
Identify hidden finite-horizon assumptions.
Identify claims that fail under alternative but reasonable resource accounting.
Identify claims sensitive to arbitrary encoding choices.
Identify claims sensitive to search algorithm rather than scientific structure.
Identify claims that are only rediscoveries of parent mathematics.
Produce a RED / AMBER / GREEN audit table for the entire corpus.
Downgrade or retract any unsupported overclaim.
Freeze an audited `GMI_THEORY_BASELINE_V1` before further upgrades.
State the minimal mathematical objects required by GMI.
Formalize machine state carriers without architecture names.
Formalize observations, actions, outputs, transformations, update channels, communication, verification, and resources.
Formalize behavioral specifications independently of implementation.
Formalize behavioral equivalence / specification equivalence.
Define minimal sufficient state and quotient constructions.
Relate GMI equivalence formally to Myhill–Nerode equivalence where applicable.
Relate it to bisimulation/state abstraction where applicable.
Relate it to sufficient statistics and predictive-state representations where applicable.
Prove exactly where those parents do and do not subsume GMI.
Formalize developmental history as a mathematical object.
Formalize developmental/search dynamics.
Formalize reachability under a developmental law.
Formalize morphology equivalence and machine-species equivalence.
Formalize capability as an architecture-independent object.
Formalize capability ceilings and impossibility regions.
Formalize lifecycle resource vectors rather than a single scalar cost.
Prove when scalarization preserves Pareto order and when it does not.
Formalize uncertainty sets/confidence objects throughout GMI.
Prove composition rules for uncertainty at the general claimed scope.
Define abstention / non-identifiability semantics globally.
Produce a compact axiom/definition set from which the rest of GMI can be derived.
Prove consistency/non-contradiction of the registered finite core where decidable.
Separate universal theorems from finite-scope theorems in the notation itself.
Define P0: named architecture supplied.
Define P1: architecture-specific property vector supplied.
Define P2: representation/operator family supplied.
Define P3: only generic computational primitives supplied.
Define P4: grammar can create/compress new primitives recursively.
Decide which levels may legitimately support `derive` language.
Require flagship known-form claims to reach at least P3 unless formally justified otherwise.
Require unseen-form claims to reach P3/P4.
Build an automated architecture-name/macros leakage detector.
Build a semantic leakage audit: detect architecture-specific operators disguised under neutral names.
Build a cost-prior audit.
Build a search-prior audit.
Build an evaluation-prior audit.
Build an ecology-selection-bias audit.

Require alternate encodings of the same semantics.
Require alternate search algorithms.
Require alternate resource scalarizations / Pareto analysis.
Define a minimal architecture-neutral grammar `G0`.
Justify every primitive in `G0` from computation/interaction requirements rather than known architectures.
Prove which known computational models `G0` can express.
Quantify description-length bias induced by `G0`.
Quantify reachability bias induced by `G0`.
Construct multiple semantically equivalent grammars with different syntax.
Test whether morphology conclusions survive grammar reminting.

Formalize the candidate machine space `M(G0, B)` under finite budget `B`.
Define semantic equivalence classes so implementation duplicates collapse.
Define morphology/species descriptors independent of architecture names.
Implement exact enumeration for small budgets.
